You will be part of a team that builds meaningful partnerships with healthcare institutions around the world, contributing to SingHealth's mission of advancing healthcare excellence beyond Singapore's borders. Leading a small team, you will drive strategic partnerships, manage a portfolio of funded projects, and ensure that SingHealth's international collaborations deliver lasting impact for all parties involved. You will oversee a portfolio of third-party funded projects, ensuring deliverables and timelines are met while coordinating resources effectively across programmes. This includes developing and refining project monitoring systems in collaboration with the team. You will develop tertiary care collaboration frameworks, coordinate complex case referral processes, manage relationships with clinical partners and monitor collaboration outcomes. Operating at the interface of user requirements, construction delivery, and government frameworks, you will support TTSH management on all matters relating to the built environment. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Design, Construction & Post-Construction Management Lead and direct the full project lifecycle across design, construction, and post-construction phases, ensuring that the developer, consultants, and contractors deliver in accordance with the approved Schedule of Accommodation, technical specifications, and master timeline. Oversee the translation of clinical requirements into engineering and architectural reality. Ensure all MEP, structural, and specialised medical systems - including medical gas, radiation shielding, and infection control infrastructure - meet international healthcare standards and regulatory requirements. Lead the TTSH technical team in monitoring site progress, identifying technical risks, and proposing mitigation strategies to prevent delays and protect the Medical Tower development timeline. Review milestone documents, design submissions, and progress reports, ensuring that all records of decisions and approvals are accurately captured for management sign-off authorities and audit-ready. Manage the technical handover process from construction to operations. Lead joint inspections with users and oversee the defects-rectification process to ensure the facility is fully fit for purpose on Day 1. Administer project contracts in accordance with PSSCOC and relevant government frameworks, including the management of variations, claims, extensions of time, and contractor obligations throughout the project lifecycle. 2. Project Management Co-own the master programme with MOHH, tracking progress against key milestones and proactively identifying risks to schedule, cost, or scope before they escalate to leadership. Lead the project governance structure, including the development secretariat function - ensuring that action logs, variation records, and approval trails are current, attributable, and aligned with MOH/H and cluster policy requirements. Maintain oversight of budget planning, capital grant documentation, and project variations, providing technical justifications and ensuring all submissions meet PSSCOC and government procurement frameworks. 3. Stakeholder Coordination Direct the requirements-gathering process across clinical users, consultants, employer's agents, and contractors, ensuring that operational and technical requirements are captured early and remain aligned through each phase of development. Guide clinical and operational users through the end-to-end planning process, facilitating productive discussions on functional design, medical equipment integration, and facilities maintenance considerations. Act as the authoritative technical voice for TTSH in huddles with MOHH and contractors, ensuring that all technical queries and site variations are resolved promptly and without compromising clinical functionality. 4. Technical Advisory Provide expert guidance to leadership on design decisions, buildability, regulatory compliance, and healthcare planning standards. Stay abreast of emerging healthcare infrastructure trends, technologies, and best practices - including advances in frailty-ready design, technology-enabled care environments, and sustainable building standards - to inform and strengthen TTSH's development direction. Undertake any other responsibilities in support of the hospital development as assigned by leadership. REQUIREMENTS Degree in Architecture, Civil & Structural, Mechanical or Electrical Engineering, Construction Management, or a related built-environment discipline. At least 18-20 years (DD) or 12-15 years (AD) of relevant experience in public sector infrastructure or major healthcare facility development. Must have seen at least one major development project through from design to practical completion. Prior experience on a public hospital project is a distinct advantage. Sound working knowledge of PSSCOC, capital grant frameworks, BCA regulations, and healthcare infrastructure standards. Demonstrated experience in contract administration, including the management of variations, claims, and extensions of time under PSSCOC or equivalent government contract frameworks. Familiarity with medical equipment planning and FFE procurement frameworks as they relate to capital grant justifications. Strong leadership capabilities with the ability to influence, guide, and align diverse stakeholders across clinical, technical, and government domains. Proven ability to co-manage complex programmes with multiple concurrent workstreams, balancing schedule, budget, and quality demands without losing governance rigour. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the credibility and composure to represent the institution at senior forums and government engagements. Highly organised, resourceful, and self-directed, with the ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy in a fast-paced and evolving project environment. It serves as the organising platform for multiple virtual and distributed care models, enabling patients to access the right care, at the right time, in the right place. Since its inception in 2020, NUHS@Home has rapidly grown into a critical pillar of NUHS’ vision for healthcare that is integrated, agile, and closer to the patient. More than a single service, it represents a new architecture for care delivery – one where geography no longer dictates access, and recovery happens where patients feel safest, supported, and most at home. The Role We are seeking an experienced, strategic and forward-thinking Senior Manager / Assistant Director, Human Resource . Reporting to the Head of Human Resource, you will serve as a trusted HR leader and strategic business partner to the NUHS@Home leadership team and key stakeholders. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who enjoys driving people strategies that support workforce transformation, talent development, employee engagement and organisational growth, while leading the HR team and providing tactical advice and practical solutions across the employee lifecycle. As a key member of the NUHS@Home leadership team, you will play an important role in shaping the people agenda and enabling the continued growth and evolution of the NUHS@Home care delivery model. You will also contribute to leadership continuity for the HR function by supporting the Head of Human Resource on designated matters and strengthening succession coverage within the HR team. What you will own Strategic HR Business Partnering Build strong, trusted relationships with business leaders and stakeholders, providing strategic advice and practical HR solutions that support organisational priorities and business outcomes. Advise leaders on the interpretation and application of HR policies and procedures, employment legislation, performance management, manpower planning, resourcing, rewards and other people-related matters. Partner with Talent Acquisition to develop and implement targeted recruitment strategies aligned with NUHS@Home manpower plans, workforce requirements and growth priorities, including the review and approval of compensation recommendations. Lead the annual manpower planning and budgeting exercise, ensuring alignment with organisational priorities, workforce requirements and financial objectives. Support organisational transformation, change management and workforce redesign initiatives to enable the growth and evolution of NUHS@Home’s care delivery model. Analyse workforce trends, employee engagement data, attrition metrics and other manpower indicators to generate insights and recommendations for organisational and workforce planning, and the effective management of organisational risks. Oversee employee lifecycle matters through the HR team, including employee enquiries, employment changes, transfers, appointments and exit processes, in accordance with HR policies and procedures. People Leadership and Development Lead, manage and develop the HR team to ensure the effective, professional and timely delivery of HR plans, programmes, processes and services. Provide direction, coaching and support to build HR capability, strengthen service delivery and promote a high-performing team culture. Foster close collaboration with relevant Group HR Centres of Excellence to deliver integrated and value-adding people solutions. Employee Engagement, Talent and Workforce Development Drive employee engagement initiatives that strengthen workplace culture, employee experience, productivity and retention. Work with leaders to identify organisational capability gaps and support organisation design, workforce planning, capability-building and talent pipeline initiatives. Promote a culture of continuous learning, collaboration, accountability and service excellence. Governance, Policy and Stakeholder Collaboration Collaborate with NUHS Group HR Centres of Excellence and relevant stakeholders to implement HR projects, programmes and initiatives. Work with the Centres of Excellence to review and enhance HR policies, guidelines and processes to ensure their relevance to NUHS@Home and compliance with applicable regulatory requirements. Contribute to NUHS, Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Ministry of Health (MOH), MOH Holdings (MOHH), NUHS@Home and Human Resource projects, events, governance initiatives, policy reviews and committees, as assigned or appointed. Who You Are This role is suited to an experienced HR leader who is able to operate at both strategic and operational levels: shaping the people agenda, advising senior stakeholders, leading a small HR team, and translating organisational priorities into practical workforce and talent solutions. Background A bachelor’s degree in Human Resource Management, Business Management or a related discipline. At least 10 years of relevant HR experience, preferably within the healthcare sector, with a strong track record in HR business partnering, organisational transformation, workforce redesign and people management. Demonstrated ability to influence and partner with business leaders to achieve strategic business and people outcomes. Demonstrated experience leading, coaching and developing HR professionals or business partners. Strong knowledge of HR practices, including employee relations, performance management, manpower planning, talent management, resourcing and rewards. Proven leadership and collaboration skills, with the ability to develop team members, build effective partnerships across functions and work independently with a high degree of initiative. Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to translate workforce data and insights into actionable recommendations. Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and PowerPoint, with experience in workforce analytics, manpower reporting, budgeting and presentation development. Experience in healthcare operations, change management or organisational capability-building would be an advantage. What we offer An opportunity to help shape NUHS’ healthcare workforce of the future and the future of healthcare delivery in Singapore. Meaningful ownership and decision-making responsibility in a high-growth healthcare transformation programme. The opportunity to contribute to the development of NUHS@Home and its future leadership capability as the programme scales. Why Join Us NUHS@Home is redefining care delivery by creating Singapore’s virtual campus for comprehensive clinical care through a digital-first approach. You will contribute to workforce transformation and the future of healthcare delivery in Singapore and beyond. jobs.title: Deputy/Assistant Director, Monetary & Domestic Markets Management Department
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 30 Oct 2026. Closing on 17 Nov 2026. The Monetary & Domestic Markets Management Department (MDD) conducts market operations to implement MAS’ monetary policy and serves as the fiscal agent of the Singapore Government. Working within a tight-knit team of high-performing officers, you will undertake foreign exchange intervention operations to manage the Singapore dollar within its policy band, money market operations to manage liquidity conditions within the banking system, and issue Singapore Government Securities. You will also be responsible for gathering market intelligence and providing updates to MAS ministers and senior management. Besides the above duties, you will be involved in a range of projects, typically working with various internal and external stakeholders including government ministries, foreign central banks, primary dealers and other market participants. Depending on the team in which you are placed, this can include: Monetary management: You will lead projects to enhance the conduct of foreign exchange and liquidity management operations, including to ensure readiness for intervention and lender of last resort functions amidst heightened financial market volatility. Domestic markets: You will drive initiatives to grow the sovereign bond market as the bedrock of Singapore’s capital markets, and participate in sovereign bond issuances. You will also explore ways to enable greater retail access to Singapore Government Securities. Markets information infrastructure: You will develop systems and data analytics solutions to support central bank operations. You will also be involved in projects to re-design processes and explore new tech solutions to improve our operations. The work is interesting and challenging. You can expect to gain: A first-hand understanding of how Singapore’s monetary policy is implemented and how government borrowings are conducted; Mandate and wherewithal to tangibly impact financial markets, the economy and the general public; The opportunity to engage with experienced industry players (e.g. banks, institutional investors in Singapore Government Securities and other domestic market participants) as well as other central bankers; and Experience across all stages of the policy life cycle, from conceptualisation to implementation. The ideal candidate: Is energetic and keen to learn, with an interest in macroeconomics, financial markets or monetary policy. Is a team player with a strong commitment to public service. Is analytical and detail oriented, with a strong grasp of numerical concepts. Has good writing, communication and presentation skills. Takes initiative and is self-driven to learn and contribute. No prior work experience or degree in economics / finance is required, as extensive training will be conducted on-the-job. Applicants should be Singapore citizens. Applicants should be prepared that they will be periodically tasked to monitor foreign exchange markets overnight as part of their operational duties. You will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and needs of stakeholders, as well as the agility to respond to changes and developments. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment. All applicants will be notified on whether they are shortlisted or not within 4 weeks of the closing date of this job posting.

jobs.jd: Posting Date: 2 Nov 2026. Closing on 16 Nov 2026. The National Security Coordination Secretariat (NSCS) is a unit under the Prime Minister's Office responsible for national security planning and coordination. NSCS partners with agencies and stakeholders to develop and co-ordinate strategies to address national security concerns. We work to secure Singapore against risks in any domain (e.g. geopolitical, economic, digital, physical, social, technological) that could compromise Singapore’s survival and success. This includes vulnerabilities to disruptions to day-to-day life, social divisions, and coercion to act against our national interest. Such risks impact multiple sectors and require multi-sector responses to effectively mitigate risks to Singapore. NSCS also works with agencies to anticipate and identify emergent security risks, and to build up capabilities and resources to deal with these. NSCS supports the Coordinating Minister for National Security, and Permanent Secretary (National Security Intelligence Coordination). The role will give you the opportunity to strengthen: o Critical Thinking: You will need to keep abreast of national security developments and synthesise information across domains (geopolitical, economic, social, environment, information, etc.) to identify and analyse cross-cutting national security risks. These include economic security risks, digital security risks, concentration risks, and inter-dependency risks. o Systems Thinking: You will need to integrate analysis of external developments with assessments of Singapore’s vulnerabilities and how the latter will change over time. You will recommend the best way to structure the Whole-of-Government response to the risk. This will require you to suggest constructive solutions which balance multiple policy considerations across domains. For specific risks, you could contribute to the full policy value-chain from strategic planning, policy formulation, policy-operations, to comms and implementation (e.g., legislation). o Influence: You will need to mobilise colleagues from a wide range of agencies, with different mandates and policy considerations, to work with you on the overall risk assessment. You will need to build consensus on the risk level Singapore can live with and the Whole-of-Government action needed to mitigate the risks. This would require you to build extensive and deep networks across domains and seniority levels, and develop a deep understanding of their considerations and constraints. Depending on your performance and experience, you could be given the opportunity to lead a team (of 2-3 officers) or project, and individually handle complex and sensitive policy pieces that cut across NSCS’s work. The policy teams in NSCS looks across: o [Policy 1] Geostrategic issues that pose existential risks to Singapore, spanning economic security, technology dependencies, manpower risks, geopolitical sensitivities, space matters, and other related issues. o [Policy 2] Critical infrastructure and interdependencies, including risks and vulnerabilities arising from the energy transition, climate change and digital dependencies. o [Policy 3] Social cohesion, resilience and public confidence, focusing on cross-cutting issues relating to social cohesion and resilience (SCR) that threaten national security, including foreign interference and influence, with a data-centric approach to drive policy shifts. You will work in a policy team / lead a policy team: o To hunt out Singapore’s cross-cutting vulnerabilities (e.g., in critical infrastructure, social resilience) that could be exploited/ disrupted and build shared risk pictures (through policy analysis and/ or data analysis) to inform decision-making by public sector leaders. o To mobilise collective Whole-of-Government efforts to tackle complex, collective-action problems. jobs.title: Assistant Director / Senior Manager (Contact Centre Ops & Planning), ServiceSG
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 3 Nov 2026. Closing on 16 Nov 2026. The operating environment of the Public Service is undergoing fundamental and rapid change. The issues we face are complex and multi-faceted, which impact the way the Public Service operates and organises itself. To prepare the Public Service for these changes, we have begun the journey towards Public Sector Transformation (PST). As part of the current phase of PST, ServiceSG aims to be on par with globally leading companies in our delivery of public services. A key transformation in the delivery of citizen services is to take a citizen-centric service journey approach to organising services in an integrated manner via a) a digital concierge via the LifeSG app, b) a physical concierge via an expanded network of Service Centres; and c) a central contact centre. Our aim is to transform the current citizen experience of having to navigate across different public agencies to an experience of the Public Service “knowing, understanding and interacting with me as One”. ServiceSG set up its first central contact centre in Aug 2022, operated by an outsourced partner, with 16 agencies onboard as users. Its wide scope and diverse operations have allowed ServiceSG to respond swiftly handle call surges within days. It has built-in levers to allow swift scale up a hired workforce whenever needed, and is working to expand the pool of manpower it could tap on, by identifying, tagging and training a group of public officers from the service delivery job role, to prepare them for immediate mobilisation to handle calls during a national emergency. By doing these, ServiceSG provides greater capacity and flexibility to manage call centre operations during a crisis, rather than relying on the call centre and/or staff capacity of one lead agency which could be overwhelmed. As Assistant Director / Senior Manager, ServiceSG Contact Centre Planning and Operations, you play a pivotal role in supporting the Director in the establishment and operationalisation of the Whole-of-Government (WOG) Resilience Community. This includes working with agency stakeholders to identify and train Public Service officers to manage high-volume, fast-paced contact centre operations, driving innovation and transformation projects, and ensuring the seamless delivery of citizen-facing services during both peacetime and crisis situations. The role also involves strategic vendor and stakeholder management, surge operations planning, and the implementation of technological solutions to enhance service delivery and productivity. jobs.jd: Posting Date: 12 Aug 2026. GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore’s Smart Nation initiatives and public sector digital transformation. As the Centre of Excellence for Infocomm Technology and Smart Systems (ICT & SS), GovTech develops the Singapore Government’s capabilities in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Application Development, Smart City Technology, Digital Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity. At GovTech, we offer you a purposeful career to make lives better where we empower our people to master their craft through robust learning and development opportunities all year round. Learn more about GovTech at tech.gov.sg. About the Role We are seeking a Deputy Director, Engineering Management to lead product engineering for a mobile-first workplace experience platform that unifies multiple employee journeys into seamless digital and physical experiences. This role presents a unique engineering leadership opportunity: owning the full vertical stack of a mobile-first workplace platform that serves the entire public service. You will lead engineering across the entire product surface: from the core mobile app that officers use daily, to essential workplace services, down to the platform APIs and SDKs that enable partner teams to publish their own digital capabilities. Rather than building standalone features in isolation, you will drive the end-to-end engineering and integration of workplace journeys that seamlessly connect digital services, shared backend systems, and physical workplace touchpoints at scale. As a senior engineering leader, you will balance technical depth, people leadership, and strategic orchestration. You will be responsible for shaping durable, reusable platform capabilities, driving engineering excellence, and actively mentoring technical talent across the broader organization. Key Responsibilities Product Engineering & Architectural Leadership: Own the technical vision across the full vertical stack, from the native mobile application and core domain microservices to extensible APIs and SDKs, while setting strict quality and security standards for both human-authored and AI-assisted code. Platform Extensibility & Integration: Drive the design of modular, reusable developer frameworks that allow partner teams across agencies to easily plug in their own capabilities, while leading the end-to-end architecture of integration-heavy journeys that bridge digital services and physical touchpoints. Cross-Functional Orchestration & Execution: Collaborate closely with Product, UX, and Operations partners to balance user experience with technical feasibility, leading internal and vendor teams to deliver reliably on platform roadmaps while maintaining high availability and low technical debt. People Leadership & Organizational Talent Growth: Foster a high-performing squad through continuous coaching, 1:1s, and clear performance standards, while actively mentoring senior engineers and emerging leaders across the wider department. Hiring & Practice Standards: Drive organizational excellence by participating actively in standard interview panels across the broader organization and feeding squad-level architectural learnings, incident post-mortems, and delivery patterns back into shared practice guidelines. What Success Looks Like Coherent Mobile Platform Experience: Public officers enjoy a seamless, resilient, mobile-first experience when accessing both core workplace services and plug-and-play partner capabilities. Thriving Developer Ecosystem: External agency teams seamlessly adopt and build upon well-architected, stable, and documented platform APIs and SDKs. Durable Technical Architecture: The platform demonstrates high availability, low technical debt, robust security, and low operational friction across all layers
